title: The fox's winter coat
description: When winter comes, a red fox does not shiver. It grows a thick, fluffy coat that keeps the cold out — like wearing its warmest jumper all season long.

body.heading: A coat that grows thicker
paragraphs: In autumn, a red fox's coat starts to change. Under the red guard hairs, a soft, dense layer of fur grows in thick and warm. By the time snow covers the ground, the fox is wearing a much fluffier coat than the sleek one it wore in summer.
The thick fur traps warm air close to the fox's skin, the way a puffy jacket traps warm air close to you. Even the fox's feet are furry, which helps it walk on cold snow.

body.heading: Made for snowy days
paragraphs: A winter fox can curl up for a nap right on the snow. Its warm coat keeps its body heat in, and it wraps its big bushy tail around its nose like a scarf.
When spring comes, the fox sheds the thick winter underfur in patches. Its coat looks scruffy for a while — then the sleek summer coat is back, ready for warm days.

takeaway: A red fox grows a thick, fluffy winter coat that traps warm air and keeps it warm in the snow — and sheds it again in spring.

safetyNotes: This is a reading activity — no outdoor trip is needed, and children should never approach a wild fox, which may bite if it feels trapped.
screenFreeExtension: Put on your own winter coat and stand outside for one minute on a cold day: which parts of you stay warmest, and where does the cold sneak in?
